questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

The plumber told Ranjit that he had fixed the leaking tap

options.text: The plumber told Ranjit, “Had he fixed the leaking tap?”
The plumber said to Ranjit, “You had fix the leaking tap.”
The plumber said to Ranjit, “I have fixed the leaking tap.”
The plumber told to Ranjit, “He had fixed the leaking tap.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The plumber said to Ranjit, “I have fixed the leaking tap.”'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence in Indirect speech.
 
• As the reported verb is 'told' then we need to change it into 'said to' also the tense of the sentence is in the past perfect tense hence, we need to use a present perfect tense.
 
• Also, the pronoun will be according to the 'Subject' i.e. 'The plumber' the receiver is 'Ranjit'
 
• Hence, the correct direct speech is Option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some of the important rules-
 
 
• In complex sentences, the past simple and past continuous may remain unchanged if the temporal relationship between the events in the clauses is clear from the context
 
• Example- John said to me, "When I got home, I went to bed straight away." (Direct speech)

 John told me that when he got home he went to bed straight away. (Indirect speech)
 
 
 
• When the reported is in the present tense then the tense of the sentence will not be changed.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

He will be leaving / home at 8 a.m. / to beating / the office rush hour.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'to beating'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Instead of using 'to beating' we need to use 'to beat'
 
• In the given sentence, we need to use an infinitive phrase instead of prepositional phrase. 
 
• We use the infinitive phrase when the action of the sentence has yet not happened or it is going to be happened soon. In the given sentence, it is clearly given that he will be leaving office as it is future prospect of the sentence. Hence, we need to use an infinitive phrase.

**So the correct sentence is-** *He will be leaving home at 8 a.m. **to beat** the office rush hour.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'**

According to J Krishnamurti, education is not about having a career but about being able to look, __observation__ and listen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Observe.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of 'observation' is incorrect instead of this we need to use Observe.
 
• In the given sentence, an infinitive phrase is used hence, we need to use a verb forms as there is a complete parallelism in the verb forms so we need to follow this completely. 
 
• The verbs 'look, observe and listen' should be in the parallel forms i.e. why observation is incorrect.

**So the correct sentence is-** *According to J Krishnamurti, education is not about having a career but about being able to look, **observe__** and listen.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

She managed the company / so well that it is made / a huge profit that year.

options.text: so well that it is made

questions.solution:
The incorrect part is **'So well that it is made'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The usage of 'is made' is incorrect instead of this we need to use 'made'
 
• The given sentence is in the past tense as we can comprehend this from the very first verb of the sentence i.e. 'managed' so we need to use a past form of the verb in the other clause as well. So the correct verb form is 'made'
 
• The usage of 'so well that' is absolutely correct as so that is a correlative pair of conjunction that means 'with the purpose that; in order that'

**Hence, the correct sentence is-** *She managed the company so well that it** made** a huge profit that year.*
